question: With which of the following Indian states is the folk dance Lezim associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lezim (Lezhim) is a vigorous, energetic folk dance of Maharashtra, traditionally performed by men using a small stringed instrument called the lezim, often as a form of physical exercise. (लेझिम नृत्य — महाराष्ट्र)

 

• It is commonly performed during festivals such as Ganesh Chaturthi processions, accompanied by drums like the dhol-tasha.

 

• The dance is characterised by rhythmic, synchronised body movements matched with the jingling sound produced by metal discs fitted on the lezim instrument, symbolising agility and community spirit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Maharashtra include Lavani, Koli (fishermen's dance), Tamasha and Dhangari Gaja.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for dances such as Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Theyyam and Thiruvathira.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 3): Known for dances such as Buiya, Ponung and Chalo.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Known for dances such as Chhau, Jhumar and Paika.

question: The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to Indian Constitution in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2002.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 11th Fundamental Duty — the duty of every parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child/ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years — was added to Article 51A of the Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. (86वां संविधान संशोधन — 2002)

 

• The same amendment simultaneously inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6-14 years.

 

• Originally the Constitution (1950) had no Fundamental Duties; Part IVA (Article 51A) with 10 Fundamental Duties was inserted later by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• There are presently 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A of the Constitution.

 

• The 42nd Amendment (1976) is also called the 'Mini-Constitution' for the scale of changes it made, including adding 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble.

 

NOTE

 

• 2000, 1970 and 2006 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these years corresponds to a constitutional amendment relating to Fundamental Duties; the 11th Fundamental Duty was specifically added in 2002 by the 86th Amendment.

question: How many delegates participated in the second session of Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 434.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The second session of the Indian National Congress was held in December 1886 at Calcutta, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, and was attended by 434 delegates. (द्वितीय अधिवेशन, कलकत्ता 1886 — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• This marked a sharp rise from the first session (Bombay, 1885, presided over by Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee), which had only 72 delegates.

 

• The growing delegate strength in these early sessions reflected the rapid spread of the Congress as an all-India political platform during its formative, Moderate phase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The third session of the INC was held at Madras (1887), presided over by Badruddin Tyabji, its first Muslim president.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the 'Grand Old Man of India', presided over the INC on three occasions: 1886 (Calcutta), 1893 (Lahore) and 1906 (Calcutta).

 

NOTE

 

• 628, 212 and 190 (Options 2, 3 and 4): These figures do not match the delegate count of the second INC session; the verified figure is 434.

question: In October 2022, ‘Tele-MANAS’ initiative was launched by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. What does ‘M’ stand for in MANAS?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mental health.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tele-MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States) was launched on 10 October 2022 (World Mental Health Day) by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. (टेली-मानस — मानसिक स्वास्थ्य)

 

• It is a toll-free, 24x7 tele-mental health helpline aimed at providing accessible mental health counselling and care across the country, especially in underserved and remote areas.

 

• The programme works through a network of state-level Tele-MANAS cells linked with existing mental health institutions and experts, and integrates with other national health helplines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tele-MANAS was launched as part of the National Tele Mental Health Programme, announced in the Union Budget 2022-23.

 

• NIMHANS Bengaluru is the nodal centre providing technical support for the programme.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorandum, Multicultural, Medicinal (Options 1, 2 and 3): None of these correctly expands 'M' in MANAS; the correct expansion is 'Mental health' (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States).

question: ‘Nupa’ dance is associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nupa Pala is a male dance form of Manipur, performed as part of the Sankirtana tradition, in which male dancers sing and dance while playing the pung (Manipuri drum) and kartal (cymbals). (नुपा पाला — मणिपुर)

 

• It is closely linked to Vaishnavite devotional traditions in Manipur and is often performed on festive and religious occasions.

 

• Manipuri Sankirtana (which includes Nupa Pala) was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable dance forms of Manipur include Ras Lila (Manipuri classical dance) and Thang-Ta (martial dance with sword and spear).

 

• Manipuri is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, alongside Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Known for Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 3): Known for Chhau, Jhumar and Paika.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Known for Bharatanatyam and Karagattam.

question: The largest wind farm cluster of India is located in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Muppandal Wind Farm in Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu, is widely cited as India's largest wind farm/wind power cluster, with an installed capacity of over 1,500 MW. (मुप्पंडल पवन फार्म — तमिलनाडु)

 

• Tamil Nadu's favourable coastal terrain along the Palghat Gap gives it some of the strongest and most consistent wind speeds in India, making the state a hub for wind energy.

 

• Tamil Nadu has historically ranked among the top states in India for installed wind power capacity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gujarat has also emerged as a major wind energy state in recent years, particularly with offshore and coastal projects, but the Muppandal cluster in Tamil Nadu remains the classic reference for 'India's largest wind farm cluster'.

 

• India ranks among the top countries in the world in total installed wind power capacity.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka (Options 1, 3 and 4): These states have significant wind power capacity, but the largest wind farm cluster (Muppandal) is located in Tamil Nadu.

question: Which of the following is a right bank tributary of the Ganga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Son.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Son River, originating near Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh, joins the Ganga near Patna (Bihar) from the south, making it a right bank tributary. (सोन नदी — गंगा की दाहिनी सहायक नदी)

 

• Right bank tributaries of the Ganga (originating from the peninsular plateau) include the Son, Punpun and Damodar (which actually joins the Hooghly).

 

• In contrast, Gomati, Gandak and Koshi all originate in or near the Himalayas and join the Ganga from the north, making them left bank tributaries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major left-bank Himalayan tributaries of the Ganga include the Ramganga, Ghaghara and Mahananda.

 

• The Koshi River is often called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent and devastating course-changing floods.

 

NOTE

 

• Gomati, Gandak and Koshi (Options 2, 3 and 4): All three are Himalayan-origin rivers that join the Ganga from the left (north) bank, not the right bank.

question: The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed in Lok Sabha on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer, as per the official answer key, is March 25, 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022, which unified the three erstwhile Municipal Corporations of Delhi (North, South and East) into a single Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), was taken up in the Lok Sabha on 25 March 2022. (दिल्ली नगर निगम संशोधन विधेयक — 25 मार्च 2022)

 

• The Bill was piloted by the Union Home Minister Amit Shah and was aimed at ensuring uniform and integrated civic administration across Delhi.

 

• It was subsequently taken up by the Rajya Sabha, and after both Houses cleared it, it received Presidential assent and became the Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Act, 2022.

 

Therefore, as per the answer key, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The unification took effect from 22 May 2022, and the first General House meeting of the unified MCD was held thereafter.

 

• Under the amended Act, the number of municipal wards in Delhi was reduced from 272 to a maximum of 250.

 

NOTE

 

• April 30, April 20 and May 15, 2022 (Options 1, 2 and 3): None of these dates correspond to the Lok Sabha's handling of this Bill in March 2022.

question: Which of the following festivals is NOT associated with Sikkim?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lohri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lohri is a winter harvest festival celebrated predominantly in Punjab and northern India (around 13 January), and is not a traditional festival of Sikkim. (लोहड़ी — पंजाब का त्योहार, सिक्किम से असंबंधित)

 

• Losar is the Tibetan/Bhutia New Year festival, widely celebrated by the Bhutia community of Sikkim.

 

• Sakewa is a major agricultural festival of the Kirat Rai community, celebrated in Sikkim and Darjeeling, while Yenya (Indra Jatra) is celebrated by the Newar community settled in Sikkim.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Sikkim include Saga Dawa, Bhumchu, Pang Lhabsol and Maghe Sankranti.

 

• Sikkim is home to a diverse mix of communities — Bhutia, Lepcha, Nepali (including Rai, Limbu, Gurung) and Newar — each with its own festivals.

 

NOTE

 

• Losar, Sakewa and Yenya (Options 1, 3 and 4): All three are festivals actively celebrated by communities within Sikkim (Bhutia, Kirat Rai and Newar respectively).

question: Identify the function of the enzyme trypsin.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Digesting proteins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Trypsin is a proteolytic (protein-digesting) enzyme secreted by the pancreas in its inactive form, trypsinogen, which is activated into trypsin in the small intestine (duodenum). (ट्रिप्सिन — प्रोटीन का पाचन)

 

• It breaks down proteins into peptides by cleaving peptide bonds, continuing the protein digestion that begins with pepsin in the stomach.

 

• Trypsin works optimally in the alkaline environment of the small intestine, unlike pepsin, which requires the acidic environment of the stomach.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other pancreatic digestive enzymes include amylase (digests carbohydrates) and lipase (digests fats).

 

• Pepsin, secreted by the stomach, is another important protein-digesting enzyme that acts before trypsin in the digestive pathway.

 

NOTE

 

• Breaking down carbohydrates (Option 2): This is the function of enzymes like amylase, not trypsin.

 

• Digesting roughage and fats (Option 3): Fats are digested by lipase; humans do not enzymatically digest roughage (dietary fibre).

 

• Emulsifying insulin (Option 4): Insulin is a hormone, not a substrate that is 'emulsified'; fat emulsification is performed by bile salts, not trypsin.

question: In India the residuary powers to legislate any matter that is NOT mentioned in the three federal lists lies with the _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is union legislature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 248 of the Indian Constitution, the residuary powers of legislation — the power to make laws on any matter not enumerated in the Union, State or Concurrent Lists (Seventh Schedule) — vest exclusively with Parliament (the Union legislature). (अवशिष्ट शक्तियाँ — संघीय विधायिका/संसद)

 

• This includes the power to impose any tax not mentioned in any of the three lists.

 

• India's allocation of residuary powers to the Union (unlike the USA, where residuary powers rest with the states) reflects the strong unitary bias built into the Indian federal system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides legislative subjects into the Union List (currently 100 subjects), State List (61 subjects) and Concurrent List (52 subjects).

 

• Examples of laws enacted using residuary powers include the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and certain cyber law/gift tax provisions.

 

NOTE

 

• Supreme Court (Option 1): It is the highest judicial body and does not hold legislative (law-making) powers.

 

• State legislature (Option 3): States legislate only on subjects in the State List and, jointly with the Union, on the Concurrent List — not on residuary matters.

 

• Respective ministry (Option 4): Ministries are executive bodies that implement laws; they do not possess independent legislative power.

question: The interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India provides overnight liquidity to banks is called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Repo rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Repo Rate (Repurchase Rate) is the interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends short-term (typically overnight) funds to commercial banks against government securities, to help them meet liquidity shortfalls. (रेपो रेट — अल्पकालिक तरलता दर)

 

• The repo rate is the RBI's key policy rate, decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), and is a primary tool used to control inflation and liquidity in the economy.

 

• A higher repo rate makes borrowing costlier for banks (and hence for the public), helping to curb inflation; a lower repo rate encourages borrowing and boosts liquidity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows funds from commercial banks, i.e., the opposite operation of the repo rate.

 

• The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate is a special overnight window (usually repo rate + a margin) that banks use to borrow from the RBI in emergency situations, against their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) securities.

 

NOTE

 

• Reverse repo rate (Option 1): This is the rate at which RBI absorbs (borrows) liquidity from banks, not the rate at which it lends liquidity to them.

 

• Marginal standing facility rate (Option 2): This is a penal, emergency overnight borrowing window for banks, distinct from the regular repo rate.

 

• Leverage rate (Option 4): This is not a recognised RBI monetary policy rate.

question: Which country is the leading producer of jute?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India is the world's largest producer of jute, accounting for the largest share of global jute output, followed by Bangladesh. (जूट उत्पादन में भारत — विश्व में अग्रणी)

 

• Within India, West Bengal is by far the leading jute-producing state, contributing the bulk of national production, followed by Bihar and Assam.

 

• Jute cultivation requires high temperature, heavy rainfall and humid climate, along with fertile alluvial soil, conditions well met in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jute is often called the 'Golden Fibre' of India due to its golden-brown colour and economic importance.

 

• India and Bangladesh together account for the overwhelming majority of the world's jute production and exports.

 

NOTE

 

• Brazil, China and Columbia (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these countries is a leading global producer of jute; production is concentrated in the Indian subcontinent, led by India.

question: Thanjavur was the capital of which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chola.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thanjavur (Tanjore), in present-day Tamil Nadu, served as the capital of the Chola dynasty, particularly under powerful rulers such as Rajaraja I and Rajendra I. (तंजावुर — चोल राजवंश की राजधानी)

 

• The magnificent Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur, built by Rajaraja I in the 11th century CE, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a masterpiece of Dravidian temple architecture.

 

• Under the Cholas, Thanjavur became a major centre of art, literature, temple architecture and administration, with the empire extending its influence across South and Southeast Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brihadeeswarar Temple, Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple and Airavatesvara Temple together form the 'Great Living Chola Temples' UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• The Cholas were also renowned for their local self-government system, evidenced by inscriptions describing village assemblies (Ur and Sabha).

 

NOTE

 

• Pala (Option 1): Their capital was at Pataliputra/Monghyr, with influence centred on Bengal and Bihar.

 

• Vakataka (Option 3): Their capital was Nandivardhana/Vatsagulma, in the Deccan region.

 

• Parmara (Option 4): Their capital was Dhar (Malwa region), in present-day Madhya Pradesh.

question: ______ is a group of cells similar in structure and function.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tissue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A tissue is defined as a group of similar cells (along with intercellular substance) that work together to perform a specific, common function. (ऊतक — समान संरचना व कार्य वाली कोशिकाओं का समूह)

 

• Tissues are broadly classified in animals into four main types: epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissue.

 

• Multiple tissues combine to form an organ (e.g., heart, stomach), and multiple organs working together form an organ system (e.g., digestive system) — representing increasing levels of biological organisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term 'tissue' was first used by the French anatomist Marie François Xavier Bichat.

 

• In plants, tissues are broadly classified into meristematic tissue (dividing cells) and permanent tissue (differentiated cells).

 

NOTE

 

• Organ system (Option 1): A group of organs working together for a common physiological function — a higher level of organisation than tissue.

 

• Organ (Option 2): A structure made of different tissues working together, not just similar cells.

 

• Molecule (Option 4): The smallest chemical unit of a substance; far below the level of cellular organisation.

question: Which law was based on notes of the music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Law of octaves.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Law of Octaves was proposed by the English chemist John Newlands in 1865, who arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass and observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, akin to the repetition of musical notes (Sa, Re, Ga, Ma...) in an octave. (न्यूलैंड्स का अष्टक नियम — संगीत के सुरों पर आधारित)

 

• This musical analogy is why it is called the 'Law of Octaves' — the eighth element resembling the first, just as the eighth musical note resembles the first note of the next octave.

 

• The law worked reasonably well for lighter elements (up to calcium) but failed for heavier elements, since Newlands assumed only 56 elements existed and left no gaps for elements yet to be discovered.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev later proposed the Periodic Law (Mendeleev's Periodic Table, 1869), arranging elements by atomic mass and leaving gaps for undiscovered elements.

 

• The Modern Periodic Law, given by Henry Moseley (1913), states that properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic number, not atomic mass.

 

NOTE

 

• Newton law (Option 1): Refers to Isaac Newton's laws of motion/gravitation, unrelated to chemical elements or music.

 

• Mendeleev law (Option 3): Based on atomic mass, arranged in a tabular periodic table — not based on musical notes.

 

• Modern periodic law (Option 4): Based on atomic number, proposed by Moseley — also unrelated to musical notes.

question: In November 2022, the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the 103 constitutional amendment providing _______ per cent reservation to people belonging to economically weaker section (EWS).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 provides 10% reservation in government jobs and educational institutions for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) among the general (unreserved) category. (103वां संविधान संशोधन — 10% EWS आरक्षण)

 

• In November 2022, in the case Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India, the Supreme Court of India, by a 3:2 majority, upheld the validity of this 10% EWS reservation, ruling that it did not violate the basic structure of the Constitution.

 

• The amendment inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) into the Constitution, empowering the State to make special provisions for the advancement of economically weaker sections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 50% ceiling on reservations laid down in the Indra Sawhney case (1992) was held by the majority not to apply to this EWS quota, since it operates outside the traditional (SC/ST/OBC) reservation framework.

 

• EWS eligibility is generally based on an annual family income limit of Rs. 8 lakh, along with land and property criteria.

 

NOTE

 

• 5, 15 and 20 per cent (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these matches the reservation percentage granted under the 103rd Amendment, which is fixed at 10%.

question: The Rural Landless Labour Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) was started in which of the following Five-Year Plans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sixth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) was launched in 1983, during the Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-85), with the objective of generating employment for the rural landless and creating durable community assets. (RLEGP — छठी पंचवर्षीय योजना, 1983)

 

• It aimed to provide at least one member of every landless rural household with wage employment for 100 days a year.

 

• RLEGP was later merged with the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) in 1989 to form the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) was also launched during the Sixth Plan, in 1980.

 

• These early rural employment schemes were later precursors to programmes such as the Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana and eventually MGNREGA (2005).

 

NOTE

 

• Seventh, Fifth and Fourth Plans (Options 2, 3 and 4): RLEGP was not launched during any of these plan periods; it was specifically launched in 1983, within the Sixth Five-Year Plan.

question: Which of the following book was written by Aryabhata?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aryabhatiyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aryabhatiyam (Aryabhatiya), composed in 499 CE, is the most famous work of the ancient Indian mathematician-astronomer Aryabhata, covering arithmetic, algebra, trigonometry and astronomy. (आर्यभटीयम् — आर्यभट्ट की रचना)

 

• In this text, Aryabhata gave an approximate value of pi (π ≈ 3.1416), explained the place value system, and proposed that the Earth rotates on its axis, causing day and night.

 

• Aryabhata worked at the ancient university of Nalanda/Kusumapura (Pataliputra) and is regarded as one of the earliest and greatest mathematician-astronomers of classical India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first satellite, launched in 1975, was named 'Aryabhata' in his honour.

 

• Later Indian astronomers such as Brahmagupta and Bhaskara I built upon and commented on the work of Aryabhata.

 

NOTE

 

• Dhatupatha (Option 1): A grammatical treatise (list of verb roots) associated with Sanskrit grammar, notably linked to Panini.

 

• Natya Shastra (Option 3): An ancient treatise on performing arts (dance, drama, music) attributed to sage Bharata Muni.

 

• Romaka Siddhanta (Option 4): One of the five ancient Siddhanta astronomical texts of India; it is not a work authored by Aryabhata himself, though he refers to such Siddhantas in his own writings.

question: Which of the following was “NOT” a main centre of Revolt of 1857?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohtak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revolt of 1857 had several major centres of resistance, but Rohtak was not one of the principal, well-known centres of the uprising in the way Kanpur, Bareilly and Lucknow were. (1857 का विद्रोह — प्रमुख केंद्र नहीं: रोहतक)

 

• Kanpur was led by Nana Sahib, assisted by Tantia Tope, and witnessed intense fighting including the Bibighar massacre.

 

• Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal, while Bareilly was a major centre led by Khan Bahadur Khan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major centres of the Revolt of 1857 included Delhi (Bahadur Shah II), Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai), Arrah (Kunwar Singh) and Faizabad (Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah).

 

• The revolt began on 10 May 1857 at Meerut and soon spread across large parts of North and Central India.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanpur, Bareilly and Lucknow (Options 1, 2 and 4): Each of these was a major, well-documented centre of the 1857 revolt, led respectively by Nana Sahib, Khan Bahadur Khan, and Begum Hazrat Mahal.

question: Which of the following river basin is present in Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahanadi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mahanadi River originates in the Chhattisgarh plateau and flows through Odisha, where it forms a large, fertile delta before draining into the Bay of Bengal. (महानदी बेसिन — ओडिशा)

 

• The Hirakud Dam, one of the longest earthen dams in the world, is built on the Mahanadi River in Odisha.

 

• The Mahanadi basin is one of the major river basins of the east-flowing peninsular rivers of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important rivers of Odisha include the Brahmani, Baitarani and Subarnarekha.

 

• The Chilika Lake, Asia's largest brackish water lagoon, lies near the mouth of the Mahanadi delta system in Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Narmada (Option 1): Flows through Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra, draining into the Arabian Sea.

 

• Krishna (Option 3): Flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Kaveri (Option 4): Flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. None of these three basins lies in Odisha.

question: 'Samvidhan Divas', is celebrated on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26th November.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Samvidhan Divas (Constitution Day) is celebrated every year on 26 November, commemorating the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly of India formally adopted the Constitution of India. (संविधान दिवस — 26 नवंबर)

 

• The day was officially designated as Constitution Day by the Government of India in 2015, to mark the 125th birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, chairman of the Drafting Committee.

 

• The Constitution, though adopted on 26 November 1949, came into full force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated separately as Republic Day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• 26 January is celebrated as Republic Day, marking the date the Constitution came into effect.

 

• 15 August is celebrated as Independence Day, marking India's independence from British rule in 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• 18th November (Option 1): Does not correspond to any constitutional milestone.

 

• 26th January (Option 2): This is Republic Day, not Constitution Day.

 

• 15th August (Option 4): This is Independence Day, not Constitution Day.

question: The first edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games was held at __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Edinburgh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Commonwealth Youth Games were held in Edinburgh, Scotland, in the year 2000. (राष्ट्रमंडल युवा खेल — पहला संस्करण, एडिनबर्ग 2000)

 

• The Commonwealth Youth Games are a multi-sport event for athletes typically aged between 14 and 18 years, held every four years among nations of the Commonwealth.

 

• The event is organised under the aegis of the Commonwealth Games Federation (CGF), the same body that oversees the main Commonwealth Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subsequent editions of the Commonwealth Youth Games have been held in cities including Bendigo (2004), Pune (2008), Isle of Man (2011), Samoa (2015) and Bahamas (2017).

 

• India hosted the 3rd Commonwealth Youth Games in Pune in 2008.

 

NOTE

 

• Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane (Options 2, 3 and 4): These Australian cities have hosted other major sporting events (including full Commonwealth Games/Olympics), but none hosted the first edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games.

question: Which of the following strokes in swimming does NOT start with a dive into the pool from outside?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Backstroke.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In competitive swimming, the backstroke is the only one of the four major strokes in which swimmers start in the water, holding the starting grips at the wall, rather than diving in from the poolside/starting block. (बैकस्ट्रोक — पानी के अंदर से शुरुआत)

 

• For backstroke starts, swimmers push off backward from the wall with their feet, since diving forward is not possible when swimming on the back.

 

• Butterfly, breaststroke and freestyle all begin with a forward racing dive from the starting blocks into the pool.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four competitive swimming strokes recognised by World Aquatics (FINA) are freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.

 

• The Individual Medley (IM) event combines all four strokes in a single race, typically in the order: butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, freestyle.

 

NOTE

 

• Butterfly, Breaststroke and Freestyle (Options 1, 3 and 4): All three strokes begin with a forward dive from outside the pool (starting blocks), unlike backstroke.

question: The chemical formula of gypsum is _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaSO₄.2H₂O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gypsum is a soft sulphate mineral with the chemical formula CaSO₄.2H₂O (calcium sulphate dihydrate). (जिप्सम — CaSO4.2H2O)

 

• When gypsum is heated (partially dehydrated) to about 150°C, it loses three-quarters of its water of crystallisation to form Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄.½H₂O).

 

• Gypsum is widely used in the manufacture of cement (as a retarder), fertilisers, and plaster of Paris, and in reclaiming alkaline (sodic) soils.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's major gypsum deposits are found in Rajasthan, Jammu & Kashmir, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat.

 

• Anhydrous calcium sulphate (without water of crystallisation, CaSO₄) is known as anhydrite.

 

NOTE

 

• CaSO₄.12H₂O and MgSO₄.12H₂O (Options 1 and 2): Neither the '12 water molecules' hydration nor magnesium sulphate corresponds to the real formula of gypsum.

 

• MgSO₄.2H₂O (Option 3): This is magnesium sulphate dihydrate (kieserite-related), not gypsum, which is a calcium (not magnesium) sulphate.
